purpose: libpng is a PNG image read/write library.

functions.png_read_info:
`png_read_info` reads and validates the PNG signature, then parses chunks up to the image-data start, filling `info_ptr` with header/info fields. Call it after creating `png_ptr`/`info_ptr`; if args are NULL it returns, and it errors on invalid chunk order (e.g., IDAT before IHDR).
Call png_read_info() only after proper libpng setup: create png_struct/info structs, establish setjmp(png_jmpbuf(png_ptr)), initialize IO with png_init_io() or a custom read function, and ensure the input source is valid and readable. If you pre-read the 8-byte PNG signature yourself, pass the exact consumed byte count to png_set_sig_bytes(); otherwise do not call png_set_sig_bytes(). Avoid forcing png_read_info() on obviously truncated/non-PNG inputs unless your error handler correctly recovers via longjmp.
functions.png_set_expand: `png_set_expand` enables libpng’s expand transforms: it marks the read pipeline to expand palette/low-bit/gray data to 8-bit grayscale or 24-bit RGB, and to add alpha if tRNS is present. It just sets flags; if transforms are already locked out, it does nothing.
functions.png_free: `png_free` frees memory allocated by `png_malloc()`. Call it with the same `png_ptr` used for allocation. If `png_ptr` or `ptr` is `NULL`, it returns immediately. If a user `free_fn` is set, that is used; otherwise it falls back to the default free.
functions.png_set_swap_alpha: `png_set_swap_alpha` enables the `PNG_SWAP_ALPHA` transform. Call it on a valid `png_structrp` before reading/writing to swap alpha position in pixel data. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it does nothing.
functions.png_set_eXIf: `png_set_eXIf` is a stub/deprecated wrapper. It does not set EXIF data; it only issues a warning: “use png_set_eXIf_1”. Call `png_set_eXIf_1` instead. `info_ptr` and `exif` are ignored.
functions.png_get_PLTE: Returns the image’s PLTE chunk data. Call with valid `png_ptr`, `info_ptr`, and `palette`; on success it sets `*palette` and `*num_palette` and returns `PNG_INFO_PLTE`. If PLTE is absent or args are null, it returns 0.
functions.png_convert_to_rfc1123: Deprecated helper to format a `png_time` as an RFC1123 date string. Call with a valid `png_structrp` and `ptime`; it returns `png_ptr->time_buffer` on success, or `NULL` if `png_ptr` is `NULL` or time is invalid (with a warning).
functions.png_error:
`png_error` reports a fatal libpng error: it may strip `#nnnn` prefixes/text per flags, then invokes libpng’s error handling and does not return. Use it for unrecoverable PNG/usage errors; pass a valid `png_ptr` and message.
Do not install an error callback that unconditionally calls abort(). Libpng expects fatal errors to transfer control via longjmp using the jmpbuf set by setjmp(png_jmpbuf(png_ptr)), or to use the default error handler. Implement the custom error_fn to longjmp to the caller's recovery point, and ensure setjmp is established before any libpng read APIs are invoked.
functions.png_set_unknown_chunks: `png_set_unknown_chunks` stores caller-supplied unknown PNG chunks in `info_ptr` for later read/write handling. Use only with valid `png_ptr/info_ptr` and `num_unknowns>0`; if unknown-chunk support is disabled for read/write, it reports an app error and returns.
functions.png_image_begin_read_from_memory: Initializes `png_image` to read a PNG from a memory buffer. Use only with `image` version `PNG_IMAGE_VERSION`, non-NULL `memory`, and `size>0`. It sets memory-backed I/O, then reads the header. Invalid args/version return an error.
functions.png_set_sPLT: `png_set_sPLT` adds one or more sPLT palette entries to `info_ptr`. Call it with valid `png_ptr`, `info_ptr`, and `entries`, and `nentries > 0`. It reallocates the palette list safely; on NULL/invalid args it returns, and on OOM/overflow it reports “too many sPLT chunks” and stops.
functions.png_set_user_limits: Sets per-reader max image width/height. Call it on a valid `png_ptr` before `png_set_IHDR()`. Images exceeding either limit are rejected; use `0x7fffffff` for effectively no limit. If `png_ptr` is NULL, it does nothing.
functions.png_set_error_fn: Sets custom error/warning handlers for a `png_struct`. Call after creating `png_ptr`; pass user context in `error_ptr`. If `png_ptr==NULL`, it does nothing. When warnings are unsupported, `warning_fn` is ignored.
functions.png_get_pixel_aspect_ratio_fixed: Returns the pixel aspect ratio as a fixed-point y/x from pHYs. Use after reading PNG info; needs non-NULL png_ptr/info_ptr and valid pHYs with positive, 31-bit x/y pixels-per-unit. Returns 0 if unavailable/invalid or division fails.
functions.png_get_x_offset_pixels: Returns the x offset from the oFFs chunk, but only if `png_ptr`/`info_ptr` are non-NULL, `PNG_INFO_oFFs` is valid, and unit type is pixels. Otherwise it returns 0. Use it after reading info.
functions.png_set_cHRM_XYZ_fixed: Sets the PNG cHRM color space from fixed-point XYZ primaries. Call with valid `png_ptr`/`info_ptr`; NULL returns immediately. It stores endpoints, marks `PNG_COLORSPACE_FROM_cHRM` on success, then syncs `info_ptr` color-space data.
functions.png_read_image: `png_read_image` reads the entire image into the caller’s row-pointer array at once. Call it after `png_read_info`/`png_read_update_info`, with `image` pointing to enough rows. It handles interlacing; if interlace handling wasn’t enabled, it warns and may fix setup.
functions.png_get_palette_max: `png_get_palette_max` returns `png_ptr->num_palette_max`, i.e. the maximum palette size supported/allowed by the PNG state. Call it with valid `png_ptr` and `info_ptr`; if either is `NULL`, it returns `-1`. `info_ptr` is checked but not used here.
functions.png_get_gAMA_fixed: `png_get_gAMA_fixed` retrieves the image’s stored gAMA value as a fixed-point gamma. Call it with valid `png_ptr`, `info_ptr`, and output ptr. It returns `PNG_INFO_gAMA` and fills `*file_gamma` only if gamma is present; otherwise returns 0.
functions.png_get_x_pixels_per_meter: Returns the X resolution from a valid pHYs chunk in pixels/meter. Use only after reading info; pass non-NULL `png_ptr`/`info_ptr`. If pHYs is absent, invalid, or unit isn’t meter, it returns 0.
functions.png_get_uint_32: `png_get_uint_32` reads a 4-byte big-endian value from `buf` and returns it as `png_uint_32`. Use it on a valid 4-byte buffer. It does no bounds checking; behavior depends on the bytes supplied.
functions.png_set_sCAL_fixed: `png_set_sCAL_fixed` stores the PNG sCAL physical scale chunk using fixed-point width/height. Use it with positive values only; invalid width/height are ignored with a warning. It converts to ASCII then calls `png_set_sCAL_s`.
functions.png_get_bit_depth: `png_get_bit_depth` returns the image’s bit depth from `info_ptr`. Call it with valid `png_ptr` and `info_ptr`; if either is `NULL`, it returns `0`. It just reads the stored metadata, no extra processing.
functions.png_get_pHYs_dpi: `png_get_pHYs_dpi` retrieves pHYs metadata: X/Y pixels-per-unit and unit type. Call it with valid `png_ptr`/`info_ptr`; outputs are filled only for non-NULL pointers. Returns `PNG_INFO_pHYs` if pHYs exists and any requested field is set, else 0.
functions.png_set_sRGB_gAMA_and_cHRM: Sets the image colorspace to sRGB and marks gAMA/cHRM for writing too. Use it with valid `png_ptr`/`info_ptr`; if either is NULL it returns. If sRGB setup succeeds, it syncs the info.
functions.png_set_check_for_invalid_index: Sets whether libpng checks for invalid palette indexes. Call it with `allowed > 0` to disable the check (`num_palette_max = 0`); otherwise it enables the check (`-1`). It just updates `png_ptr` state.
functions.png_get_hIST: `png_get_hIST` retrieves the image histogram from `info_ptr`. Call it with valid `png_ptr`, `info_ptr`, and non-NULL `hist`. If `PNG_INFO_hIST` is set, it stores `info_ptr->hist` and returns `PNG_INFO_hIST`; otherwise it returns 0.
functions.png_set_progressive_read_fn: Sets up libpng’s push/progressive reader callbacks and user data. Call once before feeding data with `png_process_data`. It stores `info_fn`, `row_fn`, `end_fn`, and installs a buffer-fill read fn. If `png_ptr` is NULL, it returns; NULL callbacks just disable those events.
functions.png_set_filter_heuristics_fixed: `png_set_filter_heuristics_fixed` is a stub/no-op in this source. It accepts filter heuristic settings for weighted PNG filtering, but here all args are unused, so calling it has no effect. Use only if your build/version implements weighted filter heuristics.
functions.png_get_cHRM_XYZ_fixed: `png_get_cHRM_XYZ_fixed` retrieves cHRM chromaticity endpoints in fixed-point XYZ form from `info_ptr`. Use it after reading/setting info; pass non-NULL output pointers you need. It returns the number of values available, or 0 if `png_ptr/info_ptr` is NULL or endpoints aren’t present.
functions.png_free_default: `png_free_default` is libpng’s default deallocator. Use it to free memory previously allocated by libpng’s default allocator. If `png_ptr` or `ptr` is `NULL`, it returns immediately; otherwise it calls `free(ptr)`. It’s deprecated.
functions.png_set_user_transform_info: Sets user-transform context for libpng’s read-side custom row transform. Call before `png_start_read_image`/`png_read_update_info`; after that it errors on reads. NULL `png_ptr` is ignored. It just stores ptr/depth/channels.
functions.png_set_cHRM_XYZ: `png_set_cHRM_XYZ` sets PNG cHRM chromaticity data from XYZ primaries. Use it with valid `png_ptr`/`info_ptr` and double XYZ values; it converts to fixed-point then calls `png_set_cHRM_XYZ_fixed`. Invalid/overflowing values are handled by `png_fixed`.
functions.png_get_sCAL_s: Returns sCAL metadata strings from `info_ptr` if `PNG_INFO_sCAL` is set. Pass valid `png_ptr`, `info_ptr`, and non-NULL output pointers; it fills `unit`, `width`, `height` and returns `PNG_INFO_sCAL`. Otherwise returns 0.
functions.png_read_end: `png_read_end` finishes reading a PNG stream after image rows: it flushes any pending IDAT/zlib state, then reads remaining chunks and validates things like palette index. Call it after `png_read_info`/`png_read_image`; if `png_ptr==NULL` it returns immediately.
functions.png_set_rgb_to_gray: `png_set_rgb_to_gray` is a convenience wrapper that sets RGB→grayscale conversion coefficients. Use it before reading/processing image data; it forwards to `png_set_rgb_to_gray_fixed` after converting `red`/`green` to fixed-point. Behavior depends on `error_action`; status can be queried with `png_get_rgb_to_gray_status`.
functions.png_set_write_user_transform_fn: Sets a write-side user transform callback. Call it with a valid `png_ptr` before writing; it marks `PNG_USER_TRANSFORM` and stores the function pointer. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it does nothing.
functions.png_malloc: `png_malloc` allocates `size` bytes using libpng’s allocator for `png_ptr`. Use it only with a valid `png_ptr`. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it returns `NULL`; if allocation fails, it calls `png_error(png_ptr, "Out of memory")` and does not return.
functions.png_set_bKGD: `png_set_bKGD` stores a PNG background color in `info_ptr` and marks `PNG_INFO_bKGD` valid. Use it with non-NULL `png_ptr`, `info_ptr`, and `background`. If any is NULL, it does nothing.
functions.png_set_chunk_cache_max: `png_set_chunk_cache_max` sets `png_ptr->user_chunk_cache_max` if `png_ptr` is non-NULL. It lets you configure the maximum chunk cache size used by libpng. If `png_ptr` is NULL, it does nothing.
functions.png_get_sRGB: Returns whether the info contains an sRGB chunk. Use with valid `png_ptr`/`info_ptr`; if `PNG_INFO_sRGB` is set and `file_srgb_intent` is non-NULL, it stores the rendering intent and returns `PNG_INFO_sRGB`. Otherwise returns 0.
functions.png_get_image_height: `png_get_image_height` returns the image height in pixels from `info_ptr->height`. Use it with valid `png_ptr` and `info_ptr`; if either is `NULL`, it safely returns `0`.
functions.png_set_gAMA_fixed: Sets the image file gamma in `info_ptr->colorspace`. Use after validating `png_ptr` and `info_ptr`; if either is NULL, it returns immediately. It calls libpng’s colorspace gamma setter, then syncs the info struct.
functions.png_set_expand_16: `png_set_expand_16` enables read-time expansion to 16-bit channels. It also forces palette→RGB and expands any tRNS chunk. Use it on `png_ptr` before reading rows. If `png_rtran_ok` fails, it does nothing; otherwise it sets `PNG_EXPAND_16 | PNG_EXPAND | PNG_EXPAND_tRNS`.
functions.png_write_end: `png_write_end` finishes a PNG stream. Call it after all IDAT data is written; it errors if no IDATs were written. If `info_ptr` is non-NULL, it may write final chunks like tIME/text and then closes out the file.
functions.png_get_rgb_to_gray_status: Returns the current RGB-to-gray conversion status from `png_ptr->rgb_to_gray_status`. Use it after setting up/performing RGB→gray conversion to inspect the result. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it returns `0`.
functions.png_set_rgb_to_gray_fixed: Sets up RGB→gray conversion with fixed-point red/green weights. Call it before read transforms; it only applies when `png_rtran_ok()` allows it and the image isn’t palette-based. `error_action` selects none/warn/error handling; status is retrievable via `png_get_rgb_to_gray_status()`.
functions.png_set_compression_strategy: Sets libpng’s zlib compression strategy and marks it as custom, disabling libpng’s dynamic strategy selection. Call it with a valid `png_structrp`; if `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it does nothing.
functions.png_process_data_skip: `png_process_data_skip` is a deprecated stub for incremental PNG input parsing. It should be called only outside `png_process_data`; it would tell the app how many input bytes to skip before the next `png_process_data` call. In current libpng it’s unimplemented, warns, and always returns 0.
functions.png_data_freer: `png_data_freer` sets/clears `info_ptr->free_me` bits to tell libpng whether the app or libpng will free specific `png_info` data. Use it only with valid `png_ptr`/`info_ptr`; `PNG_DESTROY_WILL_FREE_DATA` sets bits, `PNG_USER_WILL_FREE_DATA` clears them, else it errors.
functions.png_chunk_warning: `png_chunk_warning` reports a non-fatal libpng warning, prefixing the current chunk name when `png_ptr` is valid. Use it for chunk-related warnings. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it forwards the message directly to `png_warning`; otherwise it formats then warns.
functions.png_build_grayscale_palette: Builds a grayscale palette for indexed PNGs. Use it with a valid `png_colorp` buffer; `bit_depth` should be 1, 2, or 4. If `palette==NULL`, it returns immediately. It fills the palette with evenly spaced gray values based on bit depth.
functions.png_process_data_pause: `png_process_data_pause` is a pause hook for `png_process_data` only. Use `save!=0` to have libpng save pending input and return 0. With `save==0`, it returns remaining unprocessed bytes (minus saved buffer) so the caller can resend them.
functions.png_chunk_benign_error: `png_chunk_benign_error` reports a chunk-related error that may be treated as warning or fatal. Use it during chunk read handling. If `PNG_FLAG_BENIGN_ERRORS_WARN` is set, it calls `png_chunk_warning`; otherwise `png_chunk_error`.
functions.png_get_uint_16: `png_get_uint_16` reads a 2-byte big-endian value from `buf` and returns it as `png_uint_16`. Use it on a valid 2-byte buffer. It simply combines the two bytes; no error checking or endianness conversion beyond that.
functions.png_set_text_compression_window_bits: Sets the zlib window size for **text chunk compression**. Call it on a valid `png_ptr` before writing text. Values are clamped to **8..15**; out-of-range inputs trigger a warning and are adjusted. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it does nothing.
functions.png_image_begin_read_from_file: Design: start a PNG read from a named file, initializing `png_image` and reading the header. Use with a valid `png_image` (correct version) and non-NULL filename. Returns success/failure; on error sets an image error. Opens file in `"rb"`, owns/closes it on success.
functions.png_set_packswap: `png_set_packswap` enables byte bit-order swapping for packed pixels. Call it on a valid `png_structrp`; it only has effect when `bit_depth < 8`, setting `PNG_PACKSWAP`. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it does nothing.
functions.png_get_y_offset_inches_fixed: Returns the image’s Y offset in inches as a fixed-point value. Use it to read the stored vertical offset from `info_ptr`; it converts the Y offset from microns via `png_fixed_inches_from_microns()`. If the offset isn’t present, it follows the underlying `png_get_y_offset_microns()` behavior.
functions.png_write_rows: Writes `num_rows` image rows by calling `png_write_row` for each `*row`. `row` is a writable-typed pointer for compatibility, but only the pointed-to rows are written. If `png_ptr==NULL`, it returns immediately.
functions.png_get_oFFs: Retrieves the image oFFs chunk: x/y offset and unit type from `info_ptr`. Use only after reading info and when `PNG_INFO_oFFs` is valid. If any pointer is NULL or the chunk isn’t present, it returns 0 and leaves outputs unchanged.
functions.png_malloc_warn: `png_malloc_warn` allocates `size` bytes via libpng. Use it with a valid `png_ptr`; on success it returns the pointer. If allocation fails, it emits `png_warning(png_ptr, "Out of memory")` and returns `NULL`. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it just returns `NULL` with no warning.
functions.png_get_pixels_per_inch: Returns the image resolution in pixels/inch, derived from the stored pixels/meter value. Use it after reading PNG info via `png_ptr`/`info_ptr`. If no valid resolution is present, it returns the converted value from `png_get_pixels_per_meter` (typically 0).
functions.png_get_interlace_type: Returns the image’s interlace type from `info_ptr`. Call it with valid `png_ptr` and `info_ptr`; otherwise it returns `0`. It does not compute or modify anything—just reads the stored field.
functions.png_create_read_struct: Creates/initializes a `png_struct` for reading. Call it first, passing libpng version plus your error/warn callbacks and user data. If user memory support is off, it uses default allocation; otherwise it delegates to `png_create_read_struct_2`.
functions.png_destroy_info_struct: Frees a `png_info` object and its associated data. Call with a valid `png_ptr` and `info_ptr_ptr`; if `*info_ptr_ptr` is non-NULL, it is set to NULL first, then data is freed and the struct zeroed/freed. If `png_ptr` or `info_ptr_ptr` is NULL, it does nothing.
functions.png_set_read_user_chunk_fn: Sets a read-time callback for unknown PNG chunks. Call before reading. `user_chunk_ptr` is passed to your handler. Handler return: <0 error, 0 save chunk, >0 handled/discarded. If `png_ptr` is NULL, it does nothing.
functions.png_get_tIME: `png_get_tIME` retrieves the image’s `tIME` chunk (modification time). Call it with valid `png_ptr`, `info_ptr`, and `mod_time`; on success it stores a pointer to `info_ptr->mod_time` and returns `PNG_INFO_tIME`. Otherwise it returns 0.
functions.png_read_row: `png_read_row` reads one image row from the PNG stream. Call it after `png_read_info`/`png_read_start_row`; on first use it initializes row state. `row` gets the decoded row, `display_row` is optional for transformed/display data. If `png_ptr==NULL`, it returns.
functions.png_set_PLTE: Sets the image palette (PLTE) in `info_ptr`. Use with valid `png_ptr/info_ptr`; `num_palette` must be 0..max. For palette images, max is `1<<bit_depth` and invalid length is a fatal error; otherwise it only warns and returns.
functions.png_set_compression_mem_level: Sets zlib’s compression memory level for the PNG write/compression state. Call it with a valid `png_structrp` before compression; if `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it does nothing. It simply stores `mem_level` in `png_ptr->zlib_mem_level`.
functions.png_set_read_status_fn: `png_set_read_status_fn` sets a read-progress callback for a `png_struct`. Call it after creating `png_ptr` and before/while reading. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it does nothing. Passing `NULL` clears the callback.
functions.png_get_pixel_aspect_ratio: Returns the pixel aspect ratio from pHYs data as `y_pixels_per_unit / x_pixels_per_unit`. Use after reading info, with non-NULL `png_ptr`/`info_ptr` and `PNG_INFO_pHYs` valid. If pHYs is absent or `x_pixels_per_unit==0`, it returns `0.0`.
functions.png_set_sRGB: `png_set_sRGB` marks the image as using the sRGB colorspace and stores the rendering intent. Call it with valid `png_ptr` and `info_ptr`; otherwise it returns immediately. It updates `info_ptr->colorspace` via `png_colorspace_set_sRGB` and syncs the info struct.
functions.png_warning: `png_warning` reports a **non-fatal libpng warning**. Pass a valid `png_ptr` and message; if `warning_fn` is set it calls that, otherwise `png_default_warning`. It may strip leading `#... ` error-number text before reporting.
functions.png_chunk_error: `png_chunk_error` reports a fatal libpng error with the current chunk name prepended. Call it with a valid `png_ptr` and message; it never returns. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it falls back to `png_error(png_ptr, error_message)`.
functions.png_start_read_image: `png_start_read_image` begins row-reading setup after `png_read_update_info`. Call it once before reading image rows. If row init hasn’t happened, it calls `png_read_start_row`; if called again, it reports a duplicate-call app error.
functions.png_write_sig: Writes the PNG 8-byte file signature. Call it on a valid `png_structrp` before writing image data. It writes only the remaining bytes from `sig_bytes`; if `sig_bytes < 3`, it sets `PNG_HAVE_PNG_SIGNATURE`.
functions.png_get_header_version: Returns libpng’s header version string, including the build date/newline; if `PNG_READ_SUPPORTED` is off, it appends `"(NO READ SUPPORT)"`. `png_ptr` is unused, so it’s just for API consistency.
functions.png_convert_from_struct_tm: Converts a C `struct tm` into libpng `png_time`. Use it to fill `ptime` from `ttime`; it copies year/month/day/hour/min/sec, adjusting year by +1900 and month by +1. It does no validation or timezone handling.
functions.png_get_sCAL: `png_get_sCAL` reads the sCAL chunk from `info_ptr`. If `PNG_INFO_sCAL` is set, it fills `unit`, `width`, and `height` by converting stored strings to `double` and returns `PNG_INFO_sCAL`; otherwise returns 0. Use only when `png_ptr/info_ptr` are valid and sCAL exists.
functions.png_set_palette_to_rgb: `png_set_palette_to_rgb()` enables palette expansion: it marks the read transform to convert paletted PNGs to full RGB and also expand tRNS transparency. Call it before reading image data. If transforms are already disallowed, it does nothing.
functions.png_write_chunk: `png_write_chunk` is a thin wrapper to write one PNG chunk: it converts the 4-byte chunk name string, then calls `png_write_complete_chunk` to emit size, type, optional data, and CRC. Use it when you already have the chunk name as a string.
functions.png_handle_as_unknown: `png_handle_as_unknown` checks `chunk_name` against libpng’s chunk list and returns that chunk’s stored “keep” policy. Use it to decide whether a chunk needs special unknown-chunk handling; otherwise it returns default handling. It returns default if args are NULL or list is empty.
functions.png_set_read_user_transform_fn: Sets a read-side user transform callback. Call it on a valid `png_ptr` before reading; it enables `PNG_USER_TRANSFORM` and stores the function pointer. If read-user-transform support is off, it does nothing.
functions.png_set_compression_level: `png_set_compression_level` sets the zlib compression level in `png_ptr`. Call it with a valid `png_structrp` before writing; if `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it does nothing. It simply stores `level` in `png_ptr->zlib_level` and performs no validation.
functions.png_get_rowbytes: `png_get_rowbytes` returns `info_ptr->rowbytes`, i.e. the bytes needed for one transformed row. Call it with valid `png_ptr` and `info_ptr`; if either is `NULL`, it returns `0`. Use it to size row buffers.
functions.png_get_x_pixels_per_inch: Returns the image’s X resolution in pixels/inch, derived from the stored X pixels/meter value. Use it with `png_ptr` and `info_ptr` after reading metadata. If no X pHYs data is present, it returns 0 via the underlying getter.
functions.png_get_eXIf: `png_get_eXIf` is a deprecated stub. It always warns: “does not work; use png_get_eXIf_1”, ignores `info_ptr` and `exif`, and returns `0`. Use `png_get_eXIf_1` instead to retrieve eXIf data.
functions.png_set_compression_method: Sets the PNG zlib compression method in `png_ptr`. Use it before writing/encoding. PNG only supports method 8; other values trigger a warning, but the value is still stored. If `png_ptr` is NULL, it returns immediately.
functions.png_set_strip_16: `png_set_strip_16` enables the 16-bit→8-bit read transform. Call it on a `png_structp` before reading rows. If other read transforms are already disallowed (`png_rtran_ok` fails), it does nothing; otherwise it sets `PNG_16_TO_8`.
functions.png_set_packing: `png_set_packing` enables unpacking/packing of 1-, 2-, or 4-bit pixels to 1 byte per pixel. Call it on a valid `png_ptr` before I/O. If `bit_depth < 8`, it sets `PNG_PACK` and write-side `usr_bit_depth=8`; otherwise it does nothing.
functions.png_set_background: `png_set_background` configures read-time compositing: it replaces alpha/tRNS with a chosen background color. Call it during PNG read setup, before row processing. `background_gamma_code` selects gamma handling; `need_expand` controls expansion. It just forwards to `_fixed`.
functions.png_set_sBIT: `png_set_sBIT` stores the image’s significant-bit info in `info_ptr` and marks `PNG_INFO_sBIT` valid. Call it only with non-NULL `png_ptr`, `info_ptr`, and `sig_bit`; otherwise it does nothing. It just copies the struct, no extra validation.
functions.png_image_write_to_stdio: Writes a `png_image` to a `FILE*` stream. Use only with a valid `image` version, non-NULL `file` and `buffer`; it initializes write state, sets stdio I/O, then writes via `png_safe_execute` and frees the image. Returns success/failure.
functions.png_write_chunk_start: `png_write_chunk_start` begins writing a PNG chunk by outputting its 4-byte name and length. Use it with a valid `png_structrp`, chunk name string, and length before writing chunk data. It just forwards to `png_write_chunk_header`; no extra behavior shown here.
functions.png_set_unknown_chunk_location: Sets the location of an unknown chunk in `info_ptr`. Use it only for a valid chunk index after `png_set_unknown_chunks`. If location lacks IHDR/PLTE/AFTER_IDAT, it reports an error and coerces to IHDR or AFTER_IDAT. No action if args/index invalid.
functions.png_get_error_ptr: `png_get_error_ptr` returns the user-supplied error callback context stored in `png_ptr->error_ptr`. Use it with a valid `png_ptr` to retrieve the pointer passed to libpng’s error functions. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it returns `NULL`.
functions.png_get_y_pixels_per_inch: Returns the image’s Y resolution in pixels per inch, converting the stored pixels-per-meter value. Use it with `png_ptr` and `info_ptr` after reading image info. If no Y ppu metadata is present, it returns the converted result of that underlying value.
functions.png_write_info: Design: write the PNG header/info chunk set to the output stream. Use after initializing `png_ptr`/`info_ptr`, before image data. If `info_ptr` is NULL or `png_ptr` is NULL, it returns. It writes PLTE/tRNS and errors if a paletted image lacks a valid palette.
functions.png_process_data: `png_process_data` is the push-mode entry point for feeding newly available PNG bytes to libpng. Call it with valid `png_ptr` and `info_ptr`; it stores the input, then repeatedly processes buffered data until empty. If either pointer is NULL, it returns immediately.
functions.png_write_chunk_end: `png_write_chunk_end` finishes a chunk begun by `png_write_chunk_start()`: it writes the 4-byte CRC to the output. Call it after all chunk data is written. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it returns immediately. With I/O state support, it marks the CRC write phase before the single write.
functions.png_image_begin_read_from_stdio: Begins reading a PNG image from a `FILE*`. Use only with a valid `png_image` whose `version==PNG_IMAGE_VERSION` and a non-NULL `file`. It initializes read state, sets `io_ptr`, then reads the header. Returns 1 on success, 0 on invalid args/version or init/header failure.
functions.png_save_uint_32: `png_save_uint_32` stores a 32-bit unsigned integer into a 4-byte buffer in big-endian/network order. Use it when writing PNG chunk fields or other PNG data. It always writes 4 bytes: most-significant byte first.
functions.png_save_int_32: `png_save_int_32` stores a signed 32-bit integer into a 4-byte buffer in PNG big-endian format by casting to `png_uint_32` and delegating to `png_save_uint_32`. Use it when writing 32-bit integer values to a byte buffer.
functions.png_get_signature: `png_get_signature` returns the PNG signature bytes stored in `info_ptr`. Use it only after both `png_ptr` and `info_ptr` are valid. If either is `NULL`, it returns `NULL`. It does not read/parse data; it just exposes the saved header signature.
functions.png_get_pixels_per_meter: Returns the image resolution in pixels/meter from the pHYs chunk. Use with valid `png_ptr` and `info_ptr`; it returns `x_pixels_per_unit` only if pHYs exists, units are meters, and X==Y. Otherwise it returns 0.
functions.png_get_cHRM_fixed: `png_get_cHRM_fixed` reads cHRM chromaticity endpoints from `info_ptr` into fixed-point outputs. Use it after the chunk/colorspace is present; pass NULL for any value you don’t need. Returns `PNG_INFO_cHRM` when available, else 0.
functions.png_get_user_transform_ptr: `png_get_user_transform_ptr` returns the `user_transform_ptr` stored in `png_ptr`, or `NULL` if `png_ptr` is `NULL`. Use it to retrieve the application-defined pointer associated with libpng user transform callbacks.
functions.png_get_libpng_ver: Returns the libpng version string used to build the library. Call it with a valid `png_ptr`; it simply delegates to `png_get_header_ver(png_ptr)` and returns that string.
functions.png_set_tIME: Sets the PNG tIME chunk in `info_ptr` from `mod_time`. Use before writing the image; it does nothing if args are NULL or tIME was already written. Invalid month/day/time values are ignored with a warning.
functions.png_get_io_ptr: `png_get_io_ptr` returns the user-supplied I/O pointer (`io_ptr`) from a `png_struct`. Use it after setting custom read/write callbacks to recover your context. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it returns `NULL`.
functions.png_destroy_write_struct: Destroys a write-side libpng context and its `png_info` struct. Pass pointers to your `png_struct*` and `png_info*`; it frees associated memory and sets `*png_ptr_ptr` to `NULL`. If `png_ptr_ptr` or `*png_ptr_ptr` is `NULL`, it does nothing.
functions.png_save_uint_16: `png_save_uint_16` stores a 16-bit unsigned value into a 2-byte buffer in big-endian/network order. Use it when writing PNG data bytes. It writes `i`’s high byte to `buf[0]` and low byte to `buf[1]`; `buf` must have at least 2 bytes.
functions.png_get_valid: `png_get_valid` checks whether a given chunk flag is set in `info_ptr->valid`. Use it with non-NULL `png_ptr` and `info_ptr`; it returns `info_ptr->valid & flag`, or 0 if either pointer is NULL.
functions.png_get_current_row_number: Returns the current row being processed, mainly for user transform callbacks. For interlaced images it’s the pass sub-image row, resetting each pass. Outside callbacks it won’t fail, but results are undefined; NULL returns PNG_UINT_32_MAX.
functions.png_write_png: `png_write_png` is a convenience writer: it writes the PNG header/info and then applies requested write-time transforms before output. Use it only when `png_ptr`, `info_ptr` are valid and `info_ptr` has image rows (`PNG_INFO_IDAT`). If not, it returns or errors. Unsupported transforms trigger an app error.
functions.png_set_chunk_malloc_max: Sets libpng’s per-chunk malloc limit (`user_chunk_malloc_max`). Call it on a valid `png_ptr` to cap memory used for a single chunk. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it does nothing.
functions.png_longjmp: `png_longjmp` is libpng’s safe wrapper for `longjmp(png_ptr->jmpbuf, val)`. Use it instead of calling `longjmp` directly. If `longjmp_fn` and `jmp_buf_ptr` are set, it jumps; otherwise it calls `PNG_ABORT()`. If setjmp support is off, it aborts.
functions.png_set_gamma_fixed: Sets reader gamma correction: `screen_gamma` and `override_file_gamma` must be >0 (or special reserved flags). Call before row reading. If transforms aren’t allowed it returns; invalid gamma triggers `png_error`.
functions.png_set_flush: `png_set_flush` sets the row interval for output flushes during writing. Call it on a valid `png_ptr` before/while writing. `nrows <= 0` disables flushing; negative values are treated as 0. Null `png_ptr` is ignored.
functions.png_write_chunk_data: Writes the data payload of a chunk begun with `png_write_chunk_start()`, while updating the CRC. Use it only after starting a chunk. If `png_ptr` is NULL it returns; if `data` is NULL or `length` is 0, it does nothing.
functions.png_set_gamma: `png_set_gamma` sets the display (“screen”) gamma and file gamma used for gamma correction. Call it before reading the PNG header for best results; if called after, it overrides the file’s gamma info. Use `file_gamma` as the inverse of screen gamma.
functions.png_get_compression_type: `png_get_compression_type` returns `info_ptr->compression_type` for a valid `png_ptr` and `info_ptr`. Use it to query the image’s compression type from libpng metadata. If either pointer is `NULL`, it returns `0`.
functions.png_get_io_state: `png_get_io_state` is a read-only accessor for libpng’s current I/O state. Call it with a valid `png_ptr` during/after I/O callbacks to inspect what operation libpng is performing. It simply returns `png_ptr->io_state`; no side effects.
functions.png_access_version_number: `png_access_version_number()` returns the libpng version used to build the library (`PNG_LIBPNG_VER`). Call it with no args to query the library’s compile-time version; it just returns that 32-bit version number.
functions.png_write_info_before_PLTE: `png_write_info_before_PLTE` starts PNG output: writes the signature and IHDR, and may clear disallowed MNG features. Call it before writing PLTE/image data; if `png_ptr` or `info_ptr` is NULL it returns. Repeated calls after it already ran do nothing.
functions.png_progressive_combine_row: `png_progressive_combine_row` is for progressive display: it merges the library’s internally buffered new row into `old_row` when the callback indicates data exists. `new_row` is only a flag; if NULL, nothing happens. If `png_ptr` is NULL, it returns immediately.
functions.png_get_text: Returns text metadata from `info_ptr`. Call with valid `png_ptr`/`info_ptr`; if text exists, it stores `info_ptr->text` and count in the आउट params and returns the count. If missing/invalid, returns 0 and sets `*num_text=0` if provided.
functions.png_set_tRNS: `png_set_tRNS` stores tRNS transparency info in `png_info`/`png_struct` for later write/read handling. Call with valid `png_ptr`/`info_ptr`; pass either palette alpha bytes (`trans_alpha`,`num_trans`) or a transparent color (`trans_color`). NULL ptrs: no-op.
functions.png_get_gAMA: `png_get_gAMA` retrieves the image’s gAMA chunk value from `info_ptr`. Call it with valid `png_ptr`, `info_ptr`, and `file_gamma`; on success it stores gamma and returns `PNG_INFO_gAMA`, otherwise returns 0.
functions.png_set_text: `png_set_text` adds text chunks to `info_ptr` from `text_ptr`/`num_text`. It delegates to `png_set_text_2`; on failure it raises `png_error` with “Insufficient memory to store text”. Use it after valid `png_ptr`/`info_ptr` setup.
functions.png_set_invert_alpha: `png_set_invert_alpha` enables the `PNG_INVERT_ALPHA` transform on a `png_struct`. Call it before reading/processing image data. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it does nothing; otherwise it just sets the flag, causing alpha values to be inverted during PNG transform handling.
functions.png_get_io_chunk_type: Returns the 4-byte PNG chunk type currently being read/written (`png_ptr->chunk_name`). Use it with a valid `png_ptr` during I/O processing to inspect the active chunk. If no chunk is active, the value is whatever `chunk_name` currently holds.
functions.png_set_quantize: `png_set_quantize` enables palette quantization to reduce colors to `maximum_colors`. Use it before read/transform processing with a palette and optional histogram. If `full_quantize==0`, it only builds an index map; if `num_palette>maximum_colors`, least-used colors are dropped when `histogram` is provided.
functions.png_get_cHRM_XYZ: `png_get_cHRM_XYZ` retrieves the cHRM chromaticity endpoints in XYZ form from `info_ptr`. Call it after reading metadata; pass output pointers as needed. It returns nonzero only if `png_ptr/info_ptr` are valid and endpoints exist, otherwise 0.
functions.png_get_progressive_ptr: Returns the user I/O pointer set for progressive/push-read callbacks. Call it with a valid `png_ptr`; if `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it returns `NULL`. Use it to retrieve your app context during progressive decoding.
functions.png_get_x_offset_inches: Returns the X offset in inches from the stored micron offset. It’s a read-only helper for image placement metadata; use it after `info_ptr` is populated. It converts microns directly to float inches, so if no offset is set, it returns that underlying value converted.
functions.png_set_compression_buffer_size: Sets libpng’s compression/IDAT buffer size. Call before compression/reading uses it. `size` must be 1..PNG_UINT_31_MAX; 0/too large => `png_error`. On read structs it sets `IDAT_read_size`; on write structs, if zlib is already in use (`zowner!=0`), it warns and leaves unchanged.
functions.png_set_cHRM_fixed: `png_set_cHRM_fixed` sets PNG cHRM chromaticity data in `info_ptr` from fixed-point x/y values. Use it with valid `png_ptr`/`info_ptr`; NULL just returns. If values are accepted, colorspace is marked `FROM_cHRM` and synced into `info_ptr`.
functions.png_set_bgr: `png_set_bgr` enables the `PNG_BGR` transform so libpng treats pixel data as blue-green-red instead of red-green-blue. Call it on a valid `png_ptr` before reading/writing image data. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it does nothing.
functions.png_set_shift: `png_set_shift` enables the PNG_SHIFT transform and stores the “true” bit depths in `png_ptr->shift`. Use it before reading to expand low-bit-depth samples to full legal depths. If `png_ptr` is NULL, it does nothing.
functions.png_get_user_height_max: Returns the user-set maximum image height stored in `png_ptr`. Use it after setting/reading the PNG struct to query the limit. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it returns `0`.
functions.png_info_init_3: `png_info_init_3` is a deprecated helper to initialize a `png_info` struct, mainly for old code using default malloc/free. If the provided struct is too small, it frees it and reallocates a correct one; otherwise it zeroes the struct. Use only with a valid `png_infopp`; avoid it in new code.
functions.png_set_swap: `png_set_swap` enables byte-swapping for 16-bit PNG data. Call it on a valid `png_ptr`; if `bit_depth == 16`, it sets `PNG_SWAP_BYTES`. If `png_ptr` is NULL or depth isn’t 16, it does nothing.
functions.png_get_y_offset_inches: Returns the image’s Y offset in inches, converting the stored micron offset directly to float to avoid overflow. Use with valid `png_ptr`/`info_ptr`. It just converts `png_get_y_offset_microns`; if data is absent, behavior follows that getter.
functions.png_get_header_ver: `png_get_header_ver` returns the libpng header version string used to build the library (`PNG_LIBPNG_VER_STRING`). It ignores `png_ptr`, so it’s just for version/query checks, not state-dependent behavior. Use it to compare header vs. library versions.
functions.png_set_keep_unknown_chunks:
Sets the default policy for unknown PNG chunks. Use `keep` to choose handling; `chunk_list`/`num_chunks` can specify chunk names. `num_chunks==0` only sets the default. `num_chunks<0` means ignore all unknown chunks and most known ones except core chunks.
Yes, this crash is caused by misuse of the API. When num_chunks > 0, pass a chunk_list buffer large enough for libpng's expected layout: at least 5 * num_chunks bytes, because libpng advances through the list with chunk_list + 5*i. Do not compute capacity as sizeof(chunk_list)/4; use sizeof(chunk_list)/5 instead. Ensure each entry contains a valid 4-byte chunk name and that num_chunks does not exceed the number of complete 5-byte entries available. Alternatively, pass num_chunks <= 0 with chunk_list == NULL when no explicit list is intended.
functions.png_write_image: `png_write_image` writes a whole image from a row-pointer array. Call it after setting up `png_ptr` and image rows; for interlaced PNGs it handles all passes via `png_set_interlace_handling`. If `png_ptr==NULL`, it returns immediately.
functions.png_set_invert_mono: Sets the read-transform flag to invert 1-bit monochrome pixels. Call it on a valid `png_structrp` before reading; it does nothing if `png_ptr` is `NULL`. It only enables the transform, not the actual inversion itself.
functions.png_set_rows: `png_set_rows` stores the scanline pointer array in `info_ptr` for `png_write_png()`. Pass valid `png_ptr`, `info_ptr`, and `row_pointers`; if either struct is NULL it does nothing. Replacing existing rows frees old row data first. Non-NULL rows set `PNG_INFO_IDAT`.
functions.png_sig_cmp: `png_sig_cmp` checks whether bytes in `sig[start..]` match the PNG 8-byte signature. Use it to validate a file header; it returns `0` on match, nonzero on mismatch. `num_to_check==0` or `start>7` fail, and checks are clipped to 8 bytes.
functions.png_get_channels: `png_get_channels` returns the number of color channels in the image from `info_ptr->channels`. Call it with valid `png_ptr` and `info_ptr`; if either is `NULL`, it returns `0`. Use it to query image channel count after info is available.
functions.png_convert_to_rfc1123_buffer: Formats a `png_time` into a 29-byte RFC1123 date string. Use with a valid `out` buffer and `ptime`; returns 1 on success, 0 if `out` is NULL or fields are out of RFC1123 range.
functions.png_set_text_compression_strategy: Sets the zlib compression strategy used for text chunks. Call it with a valid `png_structrp` before writing text; if `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it does nothing. It simply stores `strategy` in `png_ptr->zlib_text_strategy`.
functions.png_get_image_width: `png_get_image_width` returns the image width in pixels from `info_ptr->width`. Call it with valid `png_ptr` and `info_ptr`; if either is `NULL`, it returns `0`. It’s a simple accessor, not a setter.
functions.png_set_scale_16: `png_set_scale_16` enables the `PNG_SCALE_16_TO_8` transform. Use it on a valid `png_structrp` before reading to request accurate 16-bit→8-bit downscaling. If read transforms aren’t allowed (`png_rtran_ok` fails), it does nothing.
functions.png_permit_mng_features: Sets which MNG features libpng may accept for this `png_struct`. Call with a valid `png_ptr`; NULL returns 0. The value is masked with `PNG_ALL_MNG_FEATURES`, stored in `mng_features_permitted`, and the permitted subset is returned.
functions.png_get_tRNS: `png_get_tRNS` retrieves tRNS transparency info from `info_ptr`. Use after reading PNG info and only if `PNG_INFO_tRNS` is valid. For palette images it returns `trans_alpha`; otherwise `trans_color`. Returns a mask indicating what was provided, or 0 if absent/invalid.
functions.png_read_update_info: `png_read_update_info` updates `info_ptr` after read transforms are set, so row/format info matches what `png_read_row` will return. Call it once before reading rows; duplicate calls after row init trigger an app error.
functions.png_get_pCAL: `png_get_pCAL` retrieves the pCAL chunk fields from `info_ptr`. Use it after reading info, with all output pointers non-NULL. If `png_ptr/info_ptr` are valid and `PNG_INFO_pCAL` is set, it fills purpose/X0/X1/type/nparams/units/params and returns `PNG_INFO_pCAL`; otherwise returns 0.
functions.png_set_expand_gray_1_2_4_to_8: `png_set_expand_gray_1_2_4_to_8` requests libpng to expand low-bit-depth grayscale images (1/2/4 bpp) to 8 bpp. Call it before reading rows. If transforms are already locked out (`png_rtran_ok` fails), it does nothing; otherwise it sets `PNG_EXPAND`.
functions.png_get_cHRM: `png_get_cHRM` retrieves chromaticity endpoints from `info_ptr` (cHRM, or from iCCP/sRGB too). Call with valid `png_ptr/info_ptr`; any output ptr may be NULL. It returns values only if endpoints exist, else nothing.
functions.png_set_sig_bytes: `png_set_sig_bytes` tells libpng how many PNG signature bytes you already consumed before calling `png_read_info`. Use it after pre-reading 0–8 bytes. `num_bytes<0` becomes 0; `>8` triggers `png_error`; `NULL` `png_ptr` is ignored.
functions.png_get_x_offset_microns: Returns the image x-offset in micrometers from `info_ptr->x_offset` only when `PNG_INFO_oFFs` is valid and `offset_unit_type == PNG_OFFSET_MICROMETER`. Otherwise it returns 0. Use after reading metadata; `png_ptr`/`info_ptr` must be non-NULL.
functions.png_set_add_alpha: `png_set_add_alpha` requests libpng to add an alpha channel by inserting a filler byte/word via `png_set_filler`. Use it on Gray/RGB images; if the filler transform is accepted, `PNG_ADD_ALPHA` is set. If `png_ptr` is NULL, it does nothing.
functions.png_get_chunk_cache_max: `png_get_chunk_cache_max` returns the current user-set max number of chunks libpng will cache. Call it with a valid `png_ptr`; if `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it returns `0`. It’s a simple getter, no side effects.
functions.png_get_x_offset_inches_fixed: Returns the X offset in inches as a fixed-point value. Use it after reading PNG info; it converts the stored X offset from microns via `png_get_x_offset_microns()`. If fixed-point support is off, it isn’t implemented.
functions.png_set_iCCP: Design: store an ICC color profile in `info_ptr` and validate/sync colorspace. Use with non-NULL `png_ptr/info_ptr/name/profile`, `compression_type==PNG_COMPRESSION_TYPE_BASE`. Bad compression errors; invalid/inconsistent profile is rejected and not copied.
functions.png_get_copyright: Returns libpng’s copyright/version text. `png_ptr` is unused and may be any valid/NULL pointer. It just returns a constant string; no state changes or errors.
functions.png_set_gray_to_rgb: `png_set_gray_to_rgb` enables a transform that converts grayscale images to RGB. Use it before reading rows. It first expands 1/2/4-bit gray to 8-bit if needed, then marks `PNG_GRAY_TO_RGB`. If row transforms aren’t allowed, it does nothing.
functions.png_set_compression_window_bits: Sets PNG compression window size for zlib. Use with a valid `png_ptr` before writing. Values are clamped to 8..15; out-of-range triggers a warning and is adjusted. `NULL` `png_ptr` does nothing.
functions.png_get_y_offset_microns: Returns the image Y offset in microns from the oFFs chunk. Use only when `png_ptr`/`info_ptr` are non-NULL and `PNG_INFO_oFFs` is valid. If the offset unit isn’t micrometers, or oFFs is absent/unsupported, it returns 0.
functions.png_set_background_fixed: Sets a read-time background-compositing transform: blends image alpha against `background_color`, strips alpha, and optionally expands before composing. Use only on read path; pass a known gamma code or it warns and returns.
functions.png_set_filter: `png_set_filter` configures which PNG row filters libpng may use when writing. Use `method=0` (`PNG_FILTER_TYPE_BASE`) and pass a bitmask of allowed filters. Invalid filter values can trigger an app error; `NULL` `png_ptr` is ignored.
functions.png_set_tRNS_to_alpha: `png_set_tRNS_to_alpha` enables expansion of a tRNS chunk into an alpha channel. Call it on a valid `png_ptr` before reading image data. If `png_rtran_ok(png_ptr, 0)` fails, it does nothing; otherwise it sets `PNG_EXPAND | PNG_EXPAND_tRNS`.
functions.png_set_longjmp_fn: Sets up/returns libpng’s internal `jmp_buf` for error handling. Call once per `png_ptr` with the `longjmp` impl and a fixed `jmp_buf_size`. Returns NULL on `png_ptr==NULL`, allocation failure, or ABI size mismatch.
functions.png_set_sCAL: `png_set_sCAL` stores the PNG sCAL physical-scale chunk. Use it with positive `width`/`height`; invalid values are ignored with a warning. It converts doubles to ASCII then calls `png_set_sCAL_s`.
functions.png_get_IHDR: `png_get_IHDR` retrieves IHDR metadata from `info_ptr` (width, height, bit depth, color, interlace, compression, filter). Pass valid `png_ptr`/`info_ptr`; any output arg may be NULL. Returns 0 if either pointer is NULL, otherwise fills fields and returns a nonzero status.
functions.png_calloc: `png_calloc` is libpng’s zero-initializing allocator. Use it with a valid `png_ptr` and requested `size`; it calls `png_malloc`, then `memset`s the block to 0 if allocation succeeds. If allocation fails, it returns `NULL`.
functions.png_set_benign_errors: Sets whether `png_benign_error()` is downgraded to a warning. Call after creating `png_ptr`: `allowed!=0` enables warnings for benign/app errors; `0` restores default error behavior.
functions.png_set_pHYs: `png_set_pHYs` stores pHYs metadata in `info_ptr`: X/Y pixels per unit and unit type. Call it with valid `png_ptr`/`info_ptr`; if either is `NULL`, it does nothing. On success it sets the fields and marks `PNG_INFO_pHYs` valid.
functions.png_set_read_fn: Replaces libpng’s default input with a user callback. Call after `png_create_read_struct`; set `io_ptr` to your stream/context, and `read_data_fn` to read bytes. If `read_data_fn==NULL`, stdio default is used when supported. Setting read+write callbacks on same struct warns and clears write.
functions.png_get_user_chunk_ptr: Returns the user-supplied `user_chunk_ptr` from `png_ptr`. Use it after setting custom chunk handling to recover your app’s context in callbacks. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it returns `NULL`.
functions.png_get_pHYs: `png_get_pHYs` retrieves the PNG physical pixel size info (x/y pixels per unit and unit type). Call it with valid `png_ptr`/`info_ptr`; outputs are filled only for non-NULL pointers. It returns `PNG_INFO_pHYs` if the chunk is present and any requested value was set, else 0.
functions.png_get_compression_buffer_size: Returns the current compression buffer size for a PNG struct. Use it with a valid `png_ptr`; if `NULL`, it returns `0`. On read structs it reports the IDAT read size, otherwise the writer’s `zbuffer_size` (or the default read size if sequential read is used).
functions.png_get_sPLT: `png_get_sPLT` retrieves the sPLT chunk data from `info_ptr`. Pass valid `png_ptr`, `info_ptr`, and `entries`; it stores the palette list in `*entries` and returns the number of palettes. If any arg is `NULL`, it returns 0.
functions.png_malloc_default: `png_malloc_default` is libpng’s built-in allocator: it ignores any app memory hook and uses `malloc` via `png_malloc_base(NULL, size)`. Use it only with a valid `png_ptr`; if `png_ptr==NULL` it returns `NULL`. On allocation failure it calls `png_error(png_ptr, "Out of Memory")` and doesn’t return normally.
functions.png_image_free: `png_image_free` releases resources owned by a `png_image` after use. Call it when you’re done with the image. It only frees if `image`, `image->opaque` are non-NULL and not in an error-handling context; otherwise it defers to safe cleanup.
functions.png_get_iCCP: Retrieves the image’s iCCP chunk data from `info_ptr`. Use only after reading PNG info; pass non-NULL `name`, `profile`, `proflen` (and optionally `compression_type`). Returns `PNG_INFO_iCCP` if present, else 0. `compression_type` is set to base; profile data returned is uncompressed.
functions.png_get_y_pixels_per_meter: Returns the Y resolution from a pHYs chunk in pixels/meter. Use only when `png_ptr` and `info_ptr` are non-NULL and `PNG_INFO_pHYs` is valid. If pHYs is absent, unsupported, or unit isn’t meters, it returns 0.
functions.png_get_eXIf_1: `png_get_eXIf_1` retrieves embedded EXIF data from `info_ptr`. Call it with valid `png_ptr`, `info_ptr`, and `exif`; on success it stores `num_exif` and the EXIF byte pointer, returning `PNG_INFO_eXIf`. If args are null or no EXIF is present, it returns 0.
functions.png_set_cHRM: `png_set_cHRM` sets the PNG cHRM chunk (white point + RGB chromaticities) in `info_ptr`. Use it before writing the image; it converts doubles to fixed-point and forwards to `png_set_cHRM_fixed`. Invalid/out-of-range values are handled by `png_fixed`/libpng error handling.
functions.png_get_color_type: Returns the image’s `color_type` from `info_ptr`. Use it only after checking both `png_ptr` and `info_ptr` are non-NULL; otherwise it returns `0`. It’s a simple accessor, not a validator.
functions.png_get_uint_31: `png_get_uint_31` reads a 32-bit big-endian value from `buf` and enforces PNG’s 31-bit unsigned limit. Use it when parsing fields that must fit in `0..PNG_UINT_31_MAX`. If the value is larger, it calls `png_error()`; otherwise it returns the value.
functions.png_set_alpha_mode_fixed: `png_set_alpha_mode_fixed` sets alpha handling for reading: it chooses the file gamma from the output gamma, validates `output_gamma` (1000..10000000), and errors if out of range. Use it before transform setup; it may adjust gamma/compose based on `mode`.
functions.png_set_sCAL_s: `png_set_sCAL_s` stores the sCAL chunk in `info_ptr` using string widths/heights. Use it with non-NULL `png_ptr/info_ptr`, `unit` 1 or 2, and valid nonempty numeric strings not starting with `-`. Invalid input triggers `png_error`; NULL `png_ptr/info_ptr` returns quietly.
functions.png_init_io: `png_init_io` sets `png_ptr->io_ptr` to a `FILE*` for libpng’s default I/O. Call it after creating `png_struct` and before read/write ops. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it returns immediately; it doesn’t do any other setup.
functions.png_set_option: Sets a per-`png_struct` option bitfield. Call with a valid `png_ptr`, even-numbered `option` in range, and `onoff` nonzero/zero to enable/disable. Returns the previous 2-bit setting; invalid args return `PNG_OPTION_INVALID`.
functions.png_set_eXIf_1: `png_set_eXIf_1` stores raw eXIf chunk data into `info_ptr`. Call it with valid `png_ptr`/`info_ptr`, byte count, and buffer; it frees any previous `info_ptr->exif`, allocates new storage, copies/records the data, and warns/returns on OOM or NULL inputs.
functions.png_get_sBIT: `png_get_sBIT` retrieves the image’s significant-bit info from `info_ptr`. Pass valid `png_ptr`, `info_ptr`, and `sig_bit`; on success it sets `*sig_bit` to `info_ptr->sig_bit` and returns `PNG_INFO_sBIT`. Otherwise it returns 0.
functions.png_set_mem_fn: `png_set_mem_fn` lets you replace libpng’s default alloc/free with your own. Call it on a valid `png_structrp` before allocations; it stores `mem_ptr`, `malloc_fn`, and `free_fn`. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it does nothing.
functions.png_set_strip_alpha: `png_set_strip_alpha` enables the read-transform `PNG_STRIP_ALPHA` on `png_ptr`, telling libpng to remove the alpha channel from input images. Call it before reading rows. If transforms are already locked out (`png_rtran_ok` fails), it does nothing.
functions.png_image_finish_read: `png_image_finish_read` completes a `png_image_begin_read` decode into `buffer`. Use it after setting `image->format`; `row_stride=0` means auto stride. It validates version and stride overflow; negative stride is allowed for reverse-row output.
functions.png_destroy_read_struct: Destroys a read-side PNG state and frees associated `png_info`/`end_info` structs. Call after reading or on error cleanup with pointers to `png_struct*` and optional info pointers. If `png_ptr_ptr` is NULL or `*png_ptr_ptr` is NULL, it returns; it also nulls `*png_ptr_ptr`.
functions.png_get_sCAL_fixed: `png_get_sCAL_fixed` reads the sCAL chunk from `info_ptr` and returns unit, width, height as `png_fixed_point`. It succeeds only if `png_ptr/info_ptr` are valid and `PNG_INFO_sCAL` is set; otherwise returns 0. It uses FP internally, so `png_get_sCAL_s` is preferred.
functions.png_create_read_struct_2: Creates a libpng read struct with optional custom error/warn handlers and custom alloc/free funcs. On success it marks the struct as read mode, sets read-specific defaults, and may enable benign/app warning behavior. Use it before any PNG read ops.
functions.png_free_data: `png_free_data` frees libpng-owned fields in `png_info` based on `mask` and `num`. Use it only with valid `png_ptr`/`info_ptr`. If `num!=-1`, it frees that text item; if `num==-1`, it frees all matching items. If pointers are NULL, it returns; if the mask isn’t set in `info_ptr->free_me`, nothing is freed.
functions.png_create_write_struct: Creates and initializes a `png_struct` for PNG writing. Use it first before write ops, passing libpng version plus optional error/warn handlers and error context. If user memory support is off, it delegates to `png_create_png_struct`; otherwise it calls `png_create_write_struct_2`.
functions.png_image_write_to_file: Writes a `png_image` to a named file by opening it in `"wb"` and delegating to `png_image_write_to_stdio`. Use with a valid `image` version, non-NULL `file_name`/`buffer`; returns 1 on success, 0 on bad args, open/write/flush/close failure.
functions.png_reset_zstream: `png_reset_zstream` resets libpng’s internal zlib inflate stream. Use it only with a valid `png_structrp`; if `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it returns `Z_STREAM_ERROR`. Otherwise it calls `inflateReset()` and returns that status. It also resets window bits to maximum.
functions.png_set_interlace_handling: Enables libpng to handle interlaced PNGs automatically. Call it before `png_read_update_info` or `png_start_read_image`. It returns 7 for interlaced images, 1 otherwise, and you still must read `image_height` rows for each pass.
functions.png_read_png: `png_read_png()` is a convenience “read-and-transform” helper: it calls `png_read_info()`, then applies requested transforms, then reads the image. Use it only after setting read transforms. If `png_ptr`/`info_ptr` are NULL it returns; huge heights error out.
functions.png_set_pCAL: `png_set_pCAL` stores a pCAL chunk in `info_ptr` for writing: calibration purpose, X0/X1, equation type, params, and units. Call only with non-NULL args; it rejects invalid `type` (<0 or >3) and invalid `nparams` (<0 or >255), reporting a write error.
functions.png_get_current_pass_number: Returns the current interlace pass number from `png_ptr->pass`. Use it after starting/while reading an interlaced PNG to know the active pass. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it returns `8` as an invalid value.
functions.png_set_filter_heuristics: Deprecated no-op. Intended to set PNG filter selection heuristics/weights for writing, but this stub ignores all args and does nothing. Use `png_set_filter_heuristics_fixed` only if supported; otherwise it has no effect.
functions.png_get_rows: `png_get_rows` just returns `info_ptr->row_pointers`, the scanline array produced by `png_read_png()`. Use it only after reading with that API and when both `png_ptr` and `info_ptr` are non-NULL; otherwise it returns `NULL`/0.
functions.png_set_crc_action: `png_set_crc_action` sets libpng’s CRC-error policy for critical and ancillary chunks. Call it on a valid `png_structp` before reading. Critical CRC errors can be left unchanged, warned+used, quiet+used, or error/quit; discard is invalid for critical data.
functions.png_write_flush: `png_write_flush` forces a sync flush of pending PNG IDAT output. Call it with a valid `png_ptr` during writing to push buffered data out. If `png_ptr` is `NULL` or all rows are already written, it returns immediately.
functions.png_create_write_struct_2: Creates a write-side `png_struct` with custom error/warn handlers and custom alloc/free hooks. Use it before any write ops; pass a matching libpng version string. On success it initializes default zlib settings; on failure returns `NULL`.
functions.png_benign_error: `png_benign_error` reports a non-fatal libpng problem. If `PNG_FLAG_BENIGN_ERRORS_WARN` is set, it emits a warning; otherwise it treats it as an error. In read mode with a current chunk, it uses chunk-specific warning/error handlers.
functions.png_read_rows: `png_read_rows` is a convenience wrapper to read multiple image rows at once. Pass arrays of row buffers (`row`) and optional display buffers (`display_row`), plus `num_rows`. If `png_ptr` is NULL it returns; if `display_row` is NULL, it reads only into `row`. It loops and calls `png_read_row` for each row.
functions.png_convert_from_time_t: Converts a `time_t` to `png_time` for PNG text/time chunks. Use by passing a valid `png_timep` and `time_t`; it calls `gmtime()` then `png_convert_from_struct_tm()`. Behavior depends on `gmtime()`—if it fails, the result is whatever that helper handles.
functions.png_set_text_compression_level: Sets the zlib compression level for non-IDAT text chunks. Call it with a valid `png_structrp` before writing text; `NULL` is ignored. It just stores `level` in `png_ptr->zlib_text_level` and does no validation.
functions.png_set_text_compression_method: Sets the zlib method for PNG text chunks. Call it with a valid `png_ptr`; if `method != 8`, libpng warns that only PNG method 8 is supported, but still stores the value in `png_ptr->zlib_text_method`.
functions.png_set_write_status_fn: Sets the write-row callback used during PNG output. Call it with a valid `png_structrp` and a function pointer, or `NULL` to clear it. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it does nothing.
functions.png_set_text_compression_mem_level: Sets the zlib memory level used for text compression. Call it with a valid `png_structrp` before writing text chunks; if `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it does nothing. It simply stores `mem_level` in `png_ptr->zlib_text_mem_level`.
functions.png_get_chunk_malloc_max: `png_get_chunk_malloc_max` returns the current per-chunk allocation limit from `png_ptr->user_chunk_malloc_max`. Use it to query the max memory libpng will allocate for a single chunk. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it returns `0`.
functions.png_get_mem_ptr: `png_get_mem_ptr` returns the user-supplied `mem_ptr` stored in `png_ptr`, or `NULL` if `png_ptr` is `NULL`. Use it to retrieve the pointer associated with custom memory allocation functions. It does not modify state.
functions.png_set_oFFs: `png_set_oFFs` stores the PNG oFFs chunk data in `info_ptr`: x/y offsets and unit type, then marks `PNG_INFO_oFFs` valid. Use it after checking `png_ptr`/`info_ptr` are non-NULL. If either is NULL, it returns without changes.
functions.png_create_info_struct: Creates and zero-initializes a `png_info` struct for a `png_ptr`. Use it after `png_create_read_struct`/`write_struct`, often before setting error handlers. Returns `NULL` if `png_ptr` is `NULL` or allocation fails; it does not raise an error.
functions.png_get_int_32: Converts 4 PNG bytes to signed `png_int_32` in big-endian order. Non-negative values return directly; negative values are decoded via 2’s complement. On invalid/overflow cases, it safely returns 0.
functions.png_get_unknown_chunks: Returns the count of unknown chunks in `info_ptr` and sets `*entries` to the stored array. Use only with non-NULL `png_ptr`, `info_ptr`, and output pointer. If any arg is NULL, it returns 0 and does not set output.
functions.png_set_filler: `png_set_filler` adds a filler byte/word to gray or RGB images. On read, it’s valid for any input if later transforms yield 8/16-bit G/RGB; on write, it sets filler placement. If read support is off, it errors.
functions.png_get_user_width_max: Returns the current user-set maximum image width from `png_ptr`. Use it to query the limit previously configured in the PNG read/write struct. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it returns `0`.
functions.png_set_alpha_mode: `png_set_alpha_mode` is a convenience wrapper: it sets alpha handling and output gamma together. Use it before reading/processing output. It just converts `output_gamma` to fixed and calls `png_set_alpha_mode_fixed`; behavior depends on `mode` and gamma constants like `PNG_DEFAULT_sRGB`.
functions.png_set_gAMA: `png_set_gAMA` sets the PNG image gamma in `info_ptr`. It’s a thin wrapper that converts `file_gamma` from `double` to libpng fixed-point via `png_set_gAMA_fixed`. Use it when you want to store gamma metadata; behavior depends on the fixed-point conversion result.
functions.png_get_y_offset_pixels: Returns the image Y offset in pixels from the oFFs chunk. Use after reading info; pass valid `png_ptr`/`info_ptr`. It returns `y_offset` only if `PNG_INFO_oFFs` is set and unit type is `PNG_OFFSET_PIXEL`; otherwise 0.
functions.png_set_invalid: `png_set_invalid` clears selected bits in `info_ptr->valid`. It’s meant to mark chunk/info data as no longer valid, especially after your app frees data that `png_free_data()` didn’t. Use only when both `png_ptr` and `info_ptr` are non-NULL; otherwise it does nothing.
functions.png_set_hIST: `png_set_hIST` stores the PNG `hIST` chunk into `info_ptr`. Use it only after `info_ptr->num_palette` is valid. If `png_ptr`/`info_ptr` is NULL or palette size is invalid, it returns/warns and skips allocation. It frees old `hIST` data first, then allocates storage.
functions.png_set_IHDR: `png_set_IHDR` sets the PNG image header in `info_ptr` (width/height, bit depth, color, interlace, compression, filter) for writing. Call it before writing image data; it checks IHDR validity and returns immediately if `png_ptr`/`info_ptr` is NULL.
functions.png_set_write_fn: Design: replace libpng’s default output/flush callbacks with user-supplied ones and store `io_ptr`. Use before writing. If `png_ptr==NULL`, it returns. `write_data_fn==NULL` falls back to default when `PNG_STDIO_SUPPORTED`; flush may be ignored if `PNG_WRITE_FLUSH_SUPPORTED` is off.
functions.png_image_write_to_memory: Writes an `png_image` to a caller buffer, or just counts required bytes if `memory==NULL`. Use only with valid `image` version, `memory_bytes` and `buffer` set. If init fails or args are bad, it returns 0; on success it fills `memory` and updates `*memory_bytes`.
functions.png_get_bKGD: `png_get_bKGD` retrieves the image’s stored bKGD background color. Call it with valid `png_ptr`, `info_ptr`, and non-NULL `background`; if `PNG_INFO_bKGD` is set, it stores a pointer to `info_ptr->background` and returns `PNG_INFO_bKGD`, else returns 0.
functions.png_get_filter_type: `png_get_filter_type` returns the image filter type stored in `info_ptr`. Call it with valid `png_ptr` and `info_ptr`; if either is `NULL`, it returns `0`. It’s a simple accessor, not a setter.
functions.png_write_row: `png_write_row` writes one image row to the PNG stream. Call it after `png_write_info()` and once per row in order; first call checks header state and init. If `png_ptr` is NULL it returns; missing `png_write_info` triggers `png_error`.
